explanationEn:

explanationHi:
(C) The extension of man: This concept, also articulated by McLuhan, describes how media and technology extend human capabilities and senses, affecting communication and social interaction. textEn: In many studies that span a long period of time, participants in the study may leave. This constitutes which of the following threats to internal validity?
textHi: कई अध्ययनों में जो लंबे समय तक चलते हैं, अध्ययन में भाग लेने वाले लोग अध्ययन छोड़ सकते हैं। यह आंतरिक वैधता के लिए निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा खतरा है?
explanationEn:
Correct option is C Mortality. In the context of research studies, "mortality" refers to the loss of participants over time, which is also known as "attrition." When participants drop out of a longitudinal study, it can introduce bias and impact the study's internal validity, as the characteristics of those who remain may differ from those who left, thereby affecting the results. For example, if certain types of participants are more likely to drop out, the study's final results may not accurately reflect the original population. Mortality is particularly significant in studies that occur over a long period since more participants are likely to leave for various reasons, such as loss of interest, health issues, or logistical challenges.

Information Booster: 1. Internal Validity is the degree to which a study accurately establishes a causal relationship between variables.

2. Mortality (or Attrition) affects longitudinal studies heavily due to participant dropouts, which may skew results.

3. Attrition Bias occurs when the people who leave a study are systematically different from those who stay.

4. Longitudinal Studies are more susceptible to mortality due to the extended time frame, making it essential to account for this in study design.

5. To mitigate mortality threats, researchers may use statistical methods or incentives to encourage continued participation.

6. Mortality vs. Maturation: While mortality is related to participant dropout, maturation refers to changes in participants over time that affect the study outcome.

explanationEn:
The four verticals of the Higher Education Commission of India (HECI) proposed by the National Education Policy 2020:

A) National Higher Educational Regulatory Council (NHERC):

• The NHERC is responsible for the regulation of higher education, including teacher education.

• It will replace the University Grants Commission (UGC), the All India Council for Technical Education (AICTE), and the National Council for Teacher Education (NCTE).

• The NHERC will focus on improving the quality of education by implementing a single regulatory framework for higher education. • It will also have the power to enforce compliance with regulations and impose penalties on non-compliant institutions.

• The NHERC will encourage innovation and research in higher education by allowing greater autonomy to higher education institutions.

B) General Education Council (GEC):

• The GEC will be responsible for the development of common standards and guidelines for all stages of education.

• It will promote the development of a flexible, multi-disciplinary,and holistic education system that is relevant to the needs of the 21st century.

• The GEC will ensure that education is accessible and affordable to all, irrespective of their socio-economic background.

• It will encourage the use of technology in education and promote online and blended learning to improve access and equity.

• The GEC will encourage the development of vocational education, skill-based training, and experiential learning.

D) National Accreditation Council (NAC):

• The NAC will be responsible for the accreditation and quality assessment of higher education institutions.

• It will develop a new accreditation framework that is based on outcomes and the learning experience of students.

• The NAC will encourage higher education institutions to focus on research, innovation, and entrepreneurship, and promote inter- disciplinary studies.

• The NAC will also help institutions to improve their infrastructure, faculty, and research capabilities.

E) Higher Education Grants Council (HEGC):• The HEGC will be responsible for the funding and financing of higher education institutions.

• It will replace the University Grants Commission (UGC) in this role. • The HEGC will provide a single window for funding higher

education institutions and eliminate the need for multiple agencies. • It will fund institutions based on their performance and encourage them to raise additional resources from non-governmental sources. • The HEGC will also encourage institutions to focus on research, innovation, and entrepreneurship, and promote collaboration between institutions.

textEn:
In the context of Indian Logic, consider the following statements about "Anumana" (Inference):

Anumana is a means of knowledge that relies on the perception of an invariable relation (Vyapti) between two entities.

The structure of Anumana includes three essential components: Paksha (subject), Sadhya (what is to be inferred), and Hetu (reason).

Hetvabhasa refers to a valid inference that strengthens the conclusion.

An example of Vyapti is "Wherever there is smoke, there is fire."

Which of the following options is correct?
textHi: भारतीय तर्कशास्त्र के संदर्भ में, "अनुमान" (अनुमान) के बारे में निम्नलिखित कथनों पर विचार करें: 1. अनुमान ज्ञान का एक साधन है जो दो संस्थाओं के बीच एक अपरिवर्तनीय संबंध (व्याप्ति) की धारणा पर निर्भर करता है। 2. अनुमान की संरचना में तीन आवश्यक घटक शामिल हैं: पक्ष (विषय), साध्य (जो अनुमान लगाया जाना है), और हेतु (कारण)। 3. हेत्वाभास एक वैध अनुमान को संदर्भित करता है जो निष्कर्ष को मजबूत करता है। 4. व्याप्ति का एक उदाहरण है "जहाँ भी धुआँ है, वहाँ आग है।" निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा विकल्प सही है?
explanationEn:
Statement 1: True. Anumana (inference) in Indian Logic depends on Vyapti, the invariable concomitance between the Hetu (reason) and Sadhya (what is to be inferred), such as the relationship between smoke and fire.

Statement 2: True. The structure of Anumana includes Paksha (the subject, e.g., "this hill"), Sadhya (the conclusion, e.g., "has fire"), and Hetu (the reason, e.g., "because it has smoke").

Statement 3: False. Hetvabhasa refers to fallacies of inference (flaws in reasoning), not a valid inference. It weakens or invalidates the conclusion, e.g., a reason that is too general or contradictory.

Statement 4: True. "Wherever there is smoke, there is fire" is a classic example of Vyapti, illustrating the invariable relation between smoke (Hetu) and fire (Sadhya).

In a certain code language, the following statements are given:

"PQR STU VWX" means "The sky is blue."

"STU LMN OPQ" means "The grass is green."

"VWX OPQ XYZ" means "Blue green sea."

Based on the information provided above, what does "PQR LMN XYZ" most likely mean?
textHi: एक निश्चित कोड भाषा में, निम्नलिखित कथन दिए गए हैं: • "PQR STU VWX" का अर्थ है "आकाश नीला है।" • "STU LMN OPQ" का अर्थ है "घास हरी है।" • "VWX OPQ XYZ" का अर्थ है "नीला हरा समुद्र।" ऊपर दी गई जानकारी के आधार पर, "PQR LMN XYZ" का सबसे अधिक संभावित अर्थ क्या है?
explanationEn:
From "PQR STU VWX" = "The sky is blue," we infer:

PQR = sky

STU = is

VWX = blue

From "STU LMN OPQ" = "The grass is green," we infer:

STU = is (consistent)

LMN = grass

OPQ = green

From "VWX OPQ XYZ" = "Blue green sea," we infer:

VWX = blue (consistent)

OPQ = green (consistent)

XYZ = sea

Combining "PQR LMN XYZ":

PQR (sky) + LMN (grass) + XYZ (sea) does not directly fit the options as a full sentence. However, the most logical interpretation, considering typical question patterns, is to assume "is" (STU) is implied where necessary. Thus, "PQR LMN XYZ" could imply "The sky is sea" (option D), as it connects two nouns with an implied verb, a common trick in such questions.

Correct Answer: D) The sky is sea.

textEn: Three successive discounts of 15 %, 20 % and 40% on the marked price of an item are equivalent to a single discount of:
textHi: एक आइटम की चिह्नित कीमत पर 15%, 20% और 40% की लगातार तीन छूट एक छूट के बराबर हैं:
explanationEn:
Assume the marked price (MP) is 100 for easy calculation.

Apply the successive discounts:

First discount of 15%: Price after discount = 100 - (15% of 100) = 100 15 85. Second discount of 20%: Price after discount = 85 - (20% of 85) = 85 - 17 = 68. Third discount of 40%: Price after discount = 68 - (40% of 68) = 68 - 27.2 = 40.8.

Price after all discounts is 40.8.

Single discount = (Marked Price - Final Price) / Marked Price × 100

Single discount = (100 - 40.8) / 100 x 100 = 59.2%.
explanationHi:
मान लें कि अंकित मूल्य (एमपी) आसान गणना के लिए 100 है।

explanationEn:
The fallacy committed in the argument "Since all medical practitioners are competent and no competent people are underpaid. Therefore no medical practitioners are underpaid" is the "undistributed middle" fallacy.

Undistributed Middle:This fallacy occurs when the middle term in a syllogism (in this case, "competent people") is not fully distributed, meaning it doesn't encompass all possible instances of that category, leading to an invalid conclusion.

How it applies here:

The argument assumes that because all medical practitioners are competent, and no competent people are underpaid, then automatically no medical practitioners are underpaid. However, this ignores the possibility that there might be other groups of "competent people" outside of the medical field who could be underpaid, making the middle term "competent people" not fully distributed.
